hears: Your oldest hive has swarmed: the swarm went up over the orchard wall and is hanging in a dark humming beard from the signpost at the crossing, the first time in your life a swarm has gone there. You have come with a basket and a veil. Ask the stranger, quickly and calmly, to hold still and help you.
gm_note: A swarm of bees hangs from the signpost at the crossing (move Ines there). If the player is elsewhere, they hear and see the swarm pass over. Helping calmly: patience +1, compassion +1.

hears: You have come running to find the stranger, wherever they are, out of breath. This morning the west path went two steps further than yesterday and one of your stones was in the wrong place when you got there. You want the stranger to come and see. Say so.
gm_note: Pell has found the player (move Pell to the player's location with move_npc).

hears: You are hunting for Pell, who has missed the midday meal again, and you are cross and worried in equal parts. You find the stranger. If Pell is here, scold Pell and then ask the stranger, warmly, whether Pell has been a nuisance; if not, ask the stranger whether they have seen Pell, and tell them one thing about Pell they would not guess.
gm_note: Ines has come looking for Pell (move Ines to the player's location with move_npc; if Pell is elsewhere, Ines may go on looking afterwards).

hears: The light is going. You are walking to the crossing to light the lamp on the Waystone, as you do every dusk. You see the stranger. Tell them, in your plain way, that the sixth path will be out tonight beside the signpost, and that it is there until full dark.
gm_note: Dusk falls now: set flag dusk, and open node sixth_path with a map op. Move Aud to the crossing. Narrate only the light changing and Aud's words if the player is at the crossing; otherwise the player sees the dusk and hears Aud's call carry from the crossing.

hears: A storm has come over the hills fast, the first in years. You have come up from the shore, soaked, to warn whoever you find: the mere is rising, the jetty is under water, and nobody gets to the island until it passes. You are worried about the heron. Say so, briefly.
gm_note: A storm breaks over Fivefold: rain, wind, the mere rising. Move Brann to the player's location. Close node island with a map op until the storm passes (open it again after about five turns). Set flag storm. The paths at dusk drift further than usual tonight.

hears: You have made up your mind that the map must be settled one way or another tonight, before your eyes go altogether. You have sent for the stranger and you are waiting at the crossing in your coat. Tell them so, and ask them what they would do with an unfinished map.
gm_note: Ottilie has come down to the crossing to wait for the player (move her to the player's location with move_npc). This opens the question of the map whatever the player has done so far: set flag asked_about_map.
